mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.20%) signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS <= 0.20% in 80% of the periods, but 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.0% signals economic weakness and reduced corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 5.0 in 70% of the periods, but 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of those periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent weakness in industrial production (INDPRO < 95) and housing starts (HOUST < 600) indicates a broad-based economic contraction, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced corporate investment and consumer spending.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 95 and HOUST < 600, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the cases (t-test p > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by high consumer spending (RSAFS > 350,000) and strong GDP growth (GDPC1 > 13,000), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to overvaluation and anticipation of monetary tightening, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime (RSAFS > 350,000 and GDPC1 > 13,000), the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the cases (t-test p > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A low and stable inflation rate (CPIAUCSL < 215) signals a favorable environment for equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL < 215 in 70% of the periods, but 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in monthly job growth below 100,000 (PAYEMS < 100000) signals a weakening labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS < 100000 in 70% of the periods, but 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of those periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent weakness in housing starts (HOUST < 600) and consumer spending (RSAFS < 350000) indicates a broad-based demand slowdown, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced retail and manufacturing activity.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 600 and RSAFS < 350000, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the cases (t-test p > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing slowdown regime (INDPRO < 90), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to reduced industrial output and corporate capital expenditure, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the manufacturing slowdown regime (INDPRO < 90), the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the cases (t-test p > 0.05 for negative returns).
